newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia carries out autopsy on Busang geologist.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia carries out autopsy on Busang geologist.

text.p: Indonesian doctors performed an autopsy on Tuesday on the body of geologist Michael de Guzman, who fell from a helicopter while flying to the Busang gold property he helped discover in East Kalimantan province.
"The preliminary autopsy has been carried out," Narciso Reyes, information attache at the Philippine Embassy in Jakarta said. "The full autopsy report will be ready within two weeks."

De Guzman, a Filipino, was chief geologist for the Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd, which estimates the Busang property to contain at least 71 million ounces of gold, the biggest find this century.

Embassy sources said an official from the Philippines consulate in Manado, North Sulawesi, was present during the autopsy, which was carried out at a public hospital in the East Kalimantan capital of Samarinda.
The sources did not rule out a further autopsy and said facilities at the Samarinda hospital were not adequate.
They said de Guzman's legal wife and two daughters were expected to arrive in Jakarta on Thursday from the Philippines.

Sugianto, chief of the airport in the East Kalimantan capital of Samarinda, said last Friday that de Guzman may have committed suicide. One of several letters found in a bag he left behind in the helicopter was addressed to his wife and said he was suffering from acute hepatitis B.

De Guzman was on his way to Busang last Wednesday when the back door of the helicopter burst open 17 minutes after leaving Samarinda airport, search and rescue officials said. Bre-X had hired the helicopter, which was said to be in good condition.

Frank Cimafranca, third secretary and consul at the Philippine Embassy, said earlier on Tuesday that de Guzman's body was likely to be shipped to the Philippines over the next few days unless police wanted to conduct further investigations.
Bre-X has entered into an an agreement with Indonesian partners and the U.S. mining giant Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc to develop Busang.

The death of de Guzman coupled with an Indonesian newspaper report last Friday that Busang contained less than the estimated gold reserves hit Bre-X share prices on the Toronto Stock Exchange last Friday, analysts said.
The shares rebounded partly on Monday after the company issued a statement defending the accuracy of the assay results and calculations on the amount of gold contained in Busang.
